about: READS the public mirror's check results back onto the publish packet (backlog 321f1409, David 2026-09-19): the machine step `read-checks` of publish-to-github v7. Runs infra/forge/read-publish-checks.sh with no packet-supplied text — the one arg it admits is the literal `--check`, its no-network input check. A run (no arg) finds the one open publish-to-github packet whose read-checks step is ready, takes the PR's head sha and url off its completed open-pr step (the sha publish-github-pr recorded when it pushed, never re-derived), reads GET /repos/algedonic-dev/boss/commits/<head>/check-runs over the PUBLIC API with no credential, takes ONE reading and never waits (backlog b81ff4ca: an in-verb wait for the CodeQL check and its Analyze (…) jobs held this host's serial runner 786 s on 2026-09-28 while eight requests queued) — a head with no check-runs yet, or with the code-scanning checks still running (Analyze (rust) took 13 minutes on both #238 and #239), is `not yet` at once, and since backlog c6cb678b so is ANY check still running: nothing completes: the partial reading goes on the packet, a running check named in still_running with no conclusion, and the verb answers `not yet` (exit 75) at once, so the runner is never held for the gate; the rule reread-publish-pr-every-15-minutes files this verb again every fifteen minutes until every check has completed, and a check still running four hours after the PR opened completes the step as `unfinished`, naming it. The step's conclusion is the verdict over EVERY check — the scan's own when it did not pass, else `failure` when any other check failed (named in `failing`) — because PR #243 closed pr-opened with its Gate red, recorded in_progress by a read that judged CodeQL alone, reads the CodeQL check-run's annotations (every page the API exposes), PATCHes the reading onto the packet's metadata as `code_scanning` — one entry per check with its conclusion, and for CodeQL the counts by rule, by file and by level — and completes read-checks with conclusion / alerts / rules. Nothing on this host is mutated and nothing on GitHub is written: the only writes are the publish packet's own reading and step, and the merge on GitHub stays David's. Measured before this verb existed: PR #238 was merged over 64 unread alerts (18 critical) on 2026-09-12 and #239 stalled on 109 (10 critical) — 100 of 100 annotations name heuristics (account_id / employee_id / uid in a log line) or #[cfg(test)] constants, and nothing inside BOSS had read either. The dispatcher rule read-publish-checks-on-read-checks-ready files this when open-pr completes; complete-publish-read-checks-on-read-publish-checks-answered reads the answer line and, on a non-zero exit, annotates the step and files the alert. The runner answers serially, so this verb is held to one reading: its timeout is the bound on a hung GET, and a GitHub that cannot be read is a FAILED line, never a not-yet. Since backlog 663589cd (David 2026-09-26, PR #244 closed red and alarmed for 22 hours) every run first asks GitHub what became of each publish PR not already read closed — open, merged or closed, the head's checks NOW while it is open, and why when it closed unmerged — and writes it onto that PR's packet as pr_state (infra/forge/publish-pr-state.sh, the pass the daily mirror-drift verb shares), so a close reaches the publish region within the rule's fifteen minutes rather than the next day.
